items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: Oh yeah, yeah, I know him well, yeah. I know him well, worked with him quite a bit, you know, in the street bands.

ctx.x: LACAZE. You want a niche or two? LACAZE. LACAZE. Yeah, I'll tell you the name is a French name, but everybody try to pronounce it in English. LACAZE, LACAZE, and the right way is LACAZE. It spells LACAZE. Does it mean something in French? Do you know what it means? No, I don't know. It's one word. Yeah, one word. That way we always, everybody, you know, when doing any business with me, they always have that one word. It's not capital. Some people use a capital C. LACAZE, but it's

one word. That is easy. You don't spell it with a capital C. LACAZE. No, no. I see, because a lot of people have your name. No, I don't know. LACAZE. Yeah, well, I don't spell that one word. Let's get your name down, too, huh? Oh, my large, that is grown. Yeah, mine is Dick Allen. And, uh... Do you say the date? Yeah, what's the date, Mr. LACAZE, I can't remember? The date? Yeah.

What's it, it is? 26? I don't remember. No, it's the 27th. Let me, I got it on my watch. It's January 27, 1972. 27. Well, uh, you know, people used to get you mixed up with Bocard. Yeah, the name is Bocard. This is, that's why I just told you about the name, LACAZE and Bocard. A lot of Bocard, uh, they called me, thought I was Peter Bocard. Yeah. Because my name is Peter and his name was Peter. But he's a Bocard and I'm LACAZE. But he know you, because he told me about you. Oh yeah, yeah, I know him well, yeah. I…
